title: Regularization Decision Tree
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Data Science
description: Walk a decision tree with the facts of six modeling problems and choose between no penalty, ridge, lasso, and elastic net, with feedback on each choice.

learningObjectives: Students will be able to choose between no penalty, ridge, lasso, and elastic net for a described modeling problem and justify the choice from the size of the data, the gap between training and validation scores, the goal, and the correlation among features.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Case-based decision making with a decision tree, hidden answers, and feedback
keyQuestions: What in the data tells you that a penalty is needed at all?
When is a model that keeps every feature the better choice?
Why is lasso a risky way to choose among highly correlated features?
commonMisconceptions: Regularization always improves a model (with no overfitting it only adds bias).
Lasso is always the best choice because it gives the simplest model (with groups of correlated features its selection is unstable).
The number of features decides the method (it guides the strength of λ, while the goal and the correlations decide the method).
assessmentOpportunities: Given a new description (500 patients, 40 lab measurements of which several are highly correlated, training R² 0.80 and validation R² 0.62, and a doctor who wants a short list of measurements to order), students name the method and the starting strength of λ and justify each step of the path.
